headline: Gas prices pushed headline inflation up. The slow-moving part of inflation held near 3%.
paragraphs: Headline CPI rose to 3.7% in September from 3.4% in August. Gasoline jumped 9.1% in the month and accounts for more than half of the increase. Gasoline is up 34% from a year ago because of the Iran war.

Strip out food and energy and core CPI is 2.6%. The Fed's preferred gauge, core PCE, is 3.0%. Shelter (up 3.2%) and services are the sticky floor. Tariff-sensitive goods have mostly faded: furniture is down from a year ago and core goods are up just 0.7%.
Watch airfares (up 22% on jet fuel) and transportation services. They show whether the energy shock is spreading into prices that stay high once they rise.
watch: Gasoline, month over month: is the shock fading?
Airfares and transportation services: is it spreading?
Rent and owners' equivalent rent: is the floor falling?
Core PCE on Oct 29: the Fed's gauge
insight: The 12-month rate will stay near 3.8% through February 2027 even if prices calm down. Last winter's index levels were held down by the shutdown and cheap gas, so the comparisons are easy. Don't read that as new inflation.
